column8: At 33 weeks with intense itching and raw skin, after trying several creams.
column9: My GP basically said pregnancy hormones can cause this, but it’s becoming unbearable.

column8: At 7 weeks vomiting every morning for hours, a week before her first OB appointment.
column9: I am 7 weeks pregnant (first OB appointment is next week) and I’m genuinely so miserable I don't even want to go to bed at night.

column8: Asking whether to seek care before her first official appointment.
column9: Did any of you go to Urgent Care or your GP for severe morning sickness before your first official appointment? Did they help you?

column8: Under 5 weeks pregnant, already applying for better-paid jobs with better benefits.
column9: I know there’s a lot to think about like parental leave etc, but am I a complete idiot for trying to take on a new role while pregnant?

column8: Her reply to advice to wait until after the baby to change jobs.
column9: But won’t it be just as hard next year when I’m caring for a newborn and not sleeping? If not now, then in two years? That’s rough

column8: First-time mother at 32 weeks told by her OB not to worry about a scan detail.
column9: Of course the minute they say don’t worry you’ll start to worry, especially with your first.

column8: Almost 13 weeks, constant low-grade nausea that has not eased.
column9: i feel so ungrateful because i havent had terrible nausea like i havent been vomiting but i constantly have low grade nausea and im almost 13 weeks now and its still there, not getting better,  and frankly my patience is wearing thin

column8: How the first trimester feels in her body.
column9: my whole body hurts. doing the smallest things feels like ive ran a marathon. im exhausted all the time and i cant believe im only 13 weeks into this. i feel terrified about the rest of the pregnancy and how im going to manage

column8: She found an error in her maternity notes before meeting her community midwife.
column9: will this incorrect info be carried through to other parts of my antenatal care?

column8: First-time mother of a 4-week-old trying to follow a schedule book loosely.
column9: I’m trying my best to softly follow the moms on call schedule (use it as a guide line) , watch wake windows, feed on demand and juggling to try to have day time naps in bassinet

column8: Other mothers and what she read disagree on bedtime.
column9: I have moms telling me I need to start at 7-7:30 instead but I read that it isn’t beneficial for newborns until 9-11.

column8: After a night up until 7am with her husband taking turns, she asks for guidance.
column9: It’s hard bc I have nothing but other peoples experiencing to go off of, so I never know if I’m doing something wrong. So I could use guidance. I never thought i would feel this defeated.

column8: The night shift she and her husband split.
column9: He’s WIDE awake at night, and my husband and I are tagging each other in because we’ve been up for so long.

column8: At 9 weeks, since announcing, parents warn her about their own children's behaviour.
column9: I’ve noticed a trend of people telling me about frustrating or annoying things their kids do and when I react, they’ll say things like “you just wait”.

column8: What bothers her about the warnings.
column9: I know my kid is going to do some fuck ass shit and we’ll probably have routines that don’t make sense to people outside of our home. I just don’t love the threat of specific behaviors coming from others.

column8: Her reply on parents competing over hardship.
column9: I find it weird that people treat parenthood competitively. Everyone is going to have their own unique struggles and that’s why I struggle with the struggle Olympics of it all lol

column8: At 16 weeks her pants no longer fit and online shops fail her.
column9: I was trying to look around to find some plus size pregnancy clothing but Amazon is continuously letting me down. I don't think it understands the fact that I'm both plus sized AND pregnant!

column8: About a big retailer's range.
column9: They have plus sized or pregnancy clothes. Nothing that fits them both....

column8: Hesitant about a smaller site a commenter suggested.
column9: I'm just concerned about giving my card info to a random site not knowing what I'll get lol.

column8: At 7 weeks, nauseous all day, before her first OB appointment.
column9: Before pregnancy, I was very active and walked a minimum of 15k steps per day and lifted weights 3 days a week. This past week, I am lucky if  even make it to 5k.

column8: At 30 weeks with her second, she has had no blood tests because of her daughter's schedule.
column9: i havent had any blood tests since i was in hospital giving birth to my daughter 😅 (its been tough to get to the clinc early enough with my daughters schedule...)

column8: Humorous vent at 32 weeks about exhaustion; earlier pregnancy at 19.
column9: I thought I was tired in the first trimester. Then it got a little better in the second. Then, I hit 32 weeks, and suddenly I need to nap every 2 hours and I’m lucky if I have the energy to do the dishes.

column8: Her advice to women earlier in pregnancy.
column9: DON’T LISTEN when people tell you it’s “too early” to nest. ITS A TRAP. DO IT NOW!

column8: Comparing this pregnancy with one at 19.
column9: Being pregnant was so much easier when I was 19 😭

column8: Late third trimester in her words.
column9: My pelvis sounds like a glow stick every time I stand up. I have the stamina of a Victorian woman with “the fainting disease”. I AM ONE INCONVENIENCE AWAY FROM CRYING IN A COSTCO PARKING LOT.

column8: At 32 weeks with nothing ready.
column9: I have nothing done or prepared even though I’m at risk for preterm labor.

column8: At 19 weeks weighing a UK summer festival at six months pregnant.
column9: There is no way I will want to sleep in a tent, so we'd have to hire a van or glamp (which hits to the tune of £800-1000 for the weekend).

column8: Why she leans towards skipping the festival.
column9: I think it's probably not worth it. I would rather save the money for my maternity leave or just get a hella good push present 😌

column8: After a weekend away that exhausted her.
column9: I think in my heart of hearts, it won't be worth it. Especially given how expensive it will be. I think I'm just mourning the loss of my past self. #motherhood

column8: On being the one whose life changes first.
column9: Also being the person for whom things change first is hard - my husband still has his normal body, can do his normal activities, can wear his normal clothes 😭

column8: Nine weeks after the birth, researching ongoing pain before her check-up.
column9: I know women tend to get fobbed off and I did in the first place so I thought maybe if I went in with some idea of what the problem might be it might get taken more seriously.

column8: She tells her boyfriend she feels unattractive; his answer.
column9: he just says I’m growing a baby, now isn’t the time to be hung up on physical appearance etc..
